findings.title: A GitHub outage holds the scheduler tick for a whole discovery cycle (about 48 min, no dispatch)
findings.detail: Scheduler.tick runs discovery synchronously and calls _dispatch only after it returns. discover.run catches GitHubReadError per target and moves on to the next target, and since 58f5742 GitHubRead._get sleeps 2+8+30 s before raising github_unavailable. With about 72 discovery-enabled targets, an API outage (5xx) or a proxy that stays down holds the tick for about 48 min per cycle. In that time no new stage is dispatched: Start work (fetch), Continue (package), vet/scout and watch all wait. Running stages in pool threads are unaffected. ossctl targets verify (verify_targets.verify) loops over the same reader and takes as long. The precondition was seen live: the round-2 runner journal at 2026-10-19 06:03:04 has discover_read_failed ConnectError for every target within tens of milliseconds. Fix: end the discovery cycle on github_unavailable (re-raise as a Deferred; Scheduler.discover keeps pending_discover or clears last_discovery and sets discover_after, e.g. 15 min), keeping github_http_<status> per target. Alternatively, add a short fail-fast breaker in GitHubRead after one exhausted retry, which also bounds targets verify. Test: three targets on a refusing transport, total sleeps <= 40 s, and a PROPOSAL_APPROVED item dispatched in the same tick.

findings.title: origin/main was advanced by a push during round 3
findings.detail: git reflog show origin/main has 'update by push' to 1981308 at 2026-10-19 08:47:10 +07, after the round-3 fix commits (07:09) and before d4e0a14 (08:49). There are at least 25 such updates since 2026-10-18 15:46. The round-3 review's 'nothing was pushed' compared main with origin/main only. The remote is the owner's own repo, history was not rewritten, and this is not a product GitHub write, but hard rule 7 forbids steps from pushing. Confirm that the pushes come from the owner or the parent session and not from a build step.
